title: Close-Up Cub
description: A brown bear peers into the window of a stopped car in Wyoming's Yellowstone National Park. The image was featured in a July 1966 National Geographic story describing the progress of Mission 66, a government effort launched in 1956 to revitalize the country's national parks after decades of increased visitation but poor maintenance. The $1 billion project concluded in 1966—a nod to its name—coinciding with the 50th anniversary of the National Park Service. The efforts of Mission 66 have had a longstanding effect on U.S. National Park infrastructure, which continues to serve millions of visitors each year.
translated_description: 一只棕熊正探头望向怀俄明州黄石国家公园内一辆停泊汽车的车窗。这张照片刊登于1966年7月《国家地理》杂志的一篇文章中，该文描述了"66号使命"计划的进展——这是美国政府于1956年启动的一项工程，旨在经过数十年游客激增却维护不善后，重振美国国家公园体系。这项耗资10亿美元的计划于1966年收官（呼应其名称中的年份），恰逢国家公园管理局成立50周年。"66号使命"的成果对美国国家公园基础设施产生了深远影响，至今仍在为每年数百万游客提供服务。
